OpenDoors is a free, independent guide for students in Classes 11–12. We map out real pathways, tell you what each one honestly requires, and don't let any institution pay to be part of the answer.

YOUR OPTION SETWIDENING —

OpenDoors is a free, independent guide that helps students in Classes 11–12 see pathways nobody's shown them. Google, YouTube and every AI assistant are great at answering a question you already know how to ask. None of them are much help with a path you've never heard of in the first place. So OpenDoors researches a small, growing set of those pathways properly: what one actually is, who it suits, what it costs in money and years, and a next step you can take this week. Two founders run it as a nonprofit, take no commission or sponsorship from any university or consultant, and it's free for students — not as an introductory offer, just free.

The real problem

Information isn't scarce. Comparable, honest options are.

Search, YouTube and AI can all answer a question you know how to ask. None of them will tell you what you should've asked instead, or what a path quietly costs the people it doesn't suit.

What search gives you

An answer to the exact question you typed, assuming you already had the right words for it.

Every source describing itself on its own terms, written to sell you rather than help you compare.

Nothing about what closes, or when.

What OpenDoors gives you

Pathways you didn't know existed, named plainly and judged on the same terms as everything else.

What one actually takes — money, years, exams — and an honest word on who it doesn't suit.

One dated, specific next step. Not another tab to leave open.

/ About
Why we exist

A place with nothing to sell you.

OpenDoors sits between a student and a set of decisions they're not really equipped to make alone. We don't educate, admit, or place anyone. We just widen what a student knows to consider, and tell the truth about what each option requires.

Who's behind it

Two founders, one non-negotiable

OpenDoors is built and run by Ashwitha and Nakshitha. It's strictly nonprofit and strictly free for students, and that's not a launch offer we'll walk back later. It's the whole point.

Our guardrails

What we will never do

These aren't values statements. They're operating rules — break either one and OpenDoors has stopped being OpenDoors.

  • No paid placement, ever. No university, consultant, or platform can pay to appear more favourably anywhere on this site.
  • Free for students, always. Nothing here will ever sit behind a paywall or a "premium" tier.
  • We say the unprofitable thing. If a pathway doesn't suit you, or the conventional choice is genuinely the right one, that's what we'll say.
  • We only publish what we can maintain. Every pathway carries a date. A handful done properly beats a hundred done carelessly.
Where we are today

Early, and honest about it

OpenDoors just went live. We've published our first pathway documents and we're out there researching more, one properly verified pathway at a time.

/ Privacy
Privacy notice · Draft, last reviewed Sep 2026

What happens to your information here

OpenDoors is built for students, and a lot of you are under 18, so we're writing this in plain language rather than legal boilerplate and being extra careful about what we collect. It follows the structure India's DPDP Act asks for (Section 5, Rule 3): an itemised list of what we collect, why, and how to undo it. It's still a draft, though. No lawyer's reviewed it yet, and a few gaps are called out honestly below instead of papered over.

Who's collecting this

OpenDoors Foundation is the Data Fiduciary for anything you submit on this site. Right now the only place we collect information at all is the . No accounts, no logins, nothing else on the site asks you for anything.

Exactly what we collect, and why

What you give usWhy we need it
Your nameSo a founder can address you properly in the reply.
Your email or WhatsApp numberThe only way we have to send back an answer — we don't use it for anything else.
Your stream (Science/Commerce/Humanities/not sure)So the answer's relevant to your subjects.
Whatever you write in "your situation"The actual content we need to answer your question — class, board, state, what you're deciding between, all optional beyond what you choose to share.

That's the complete list. We don't collect location, device data, browsing history, or anything passively — there's no tracking script on this site to collect it with.

Consent

The Ask Us form only submits once you've separately ticked that you agree to this notice, and confirmed either you're 18+ or a parent/guardian is aware. Both boxes start unticked — nothing is assumed on your behalf. You can withdraw consent at any time by asking us to delete your data (see below); it's exactly as easy as giving it.

What we don't do

  • No selling or sharing your data. Nothing you submit goes to universities, advertisers, or any third party.
  • No targeted advertising. There are no ad networks on this site, and there never will be aimed at students.
  • No behavioural tracking. We're not profiling how you browse or building an ad profile of you.
  • No data kept longer than needed. We aim to delete your submission within 90 days of answering it, sooner if you ask.

Since most of you are under 18

India's DPDP Act has specific, stricter rules for anyone under 18 — including verified parental consent, using proper ID or age-verification technology, before processing a minor's data. We're honest that we don't have that verification infrastructure yet: today, the age/guardian-awareness checkbox on the form is a self-declaration, not a verified one. Treat this as a gap we know about and are building toward, not a claim that we've already solved it. In the meantime, we still hold ourselves to the substance of the child-data rules that don't need verification tech: no tracking, no targeted ads, no profiling, minimal collection — those apply in full, today.

Your rights over your own data

  • Access. Ask what we hold on you and we'll show you everything, in full.
  • Correction. Ask us to fix anything inaccurate or outdated.
  • Erasure. Ask us to delete your data entirely, at any time, for any reason.
  • Withdraw consent. Same effect as erasure — we stop holding your data.
  • Grievance redressal. If you're unhappy with how a request was handled, tell us that too — we treat it as a separate, escalated ask.

All of these go through one place right now — the — since we're small enough that a dedicated grievance officer or ticket system would be theatre, not substance. We aim to act within 7 days. As OpenDoors grows past a two-person team, a named grievance contact will replace this.

Language

This notice is currently in English only. DPDP asks for notices to be available in English or any of the 22 scheduled Indian languages — that's a real gap for a national student audience, and one of the first things we'll fix as OpenDoors grows.

If this changes

As OpenDoors grows — logins, saved shortlists, anything that needs more data — this page gets rewritten first, not after. We'll date every version so it's obvious when something changed.

/ Terms of use
Terms of use · Draft, last reviewed Sep 2026

The fine print, written like we mean it

This covers what OpenDoors is, what it isn't, and what happens if something on here turns out to be wrong. Like the Privacy Notice, this is a draft — not yet reviewed by a lawyer — written now because a student using this site deserves to know where they stand, not because we're waiting for a legal deadline.

What OpenDoors is

A free, independent information resource for students in Classes 11–12 researching degrees, exams, and countries. That's it. Using this site means you've read and agree to these terms — if you don't agree, the only ask we have is that you not use the site.

What OpenDoors is not

  • Not certified career counseling. Nobody answering your question on the Ask Us page holds a professional counseling licence. It's informed opinion from people who've researched your situation, not a substitute for a qualified counselor, and definitely not legal, financial, or medical advice.
  • Not a guarantee of admission, rank, or outcome. Nothing here promises you'll get into a university, clear a cutoff, or that a pathway will work out the way it's described.
  • Not an official source. For anything that decides your actual eligibility or application — cutoffs, deadlines, fees — the university's or exam board's own site is the authority, not us. We link to those sources specifically so you can verify.

Accuracy — what we promise, and what we can't

We research before we publish, and we date what we can. But exam cutoffs, rankings, and admission rules change — sometimes every year, sometimes mid-year. Where we genuinely don't have researched data (most of the university database, honestly), we say "Not yet researched" instead of guessing. Where we do show a number, treat it as a strong starting point to verify, not a final answer to act on unchecked.

Links to other sites

We link out to places like Internshala, EC Database, university admissions pages, and various YouTube channels and exam boards. We don't run those sites, can't vouch for everything on them, and aren't responsible for what happens once you click through. We link to them because we think they're genuinely useful — not because we're paid to (we never are).

If you're under 18

Most people using this site are. Nothing here requires payment, an account, or handing over more information than the Ask Us form asks for — see the for exactly what that is and why. If a parent or guardian has questions about what their kid submitted here, we'll answer them directly — just say so when you reach out.

Content and reuse

Everything OpenDoors writes is free to read, share, and link to. If you want to republish or reuse it elsewhere, credit OpenDoors and link back — we're not precious about it, we just don't want our research showing up somewhere with the honesty edited out.

If something's wrong

Tell us. Outdated cutoffs, a broken link, a rude answer from us — whatever it is, the is the fastest way to reach an actual founder, not a support queue. We'll fix genuine errors and treat every correction as making the site better for the next student who reads that page.

/ Resources
Resources · exams & creators

Where to actually look, not just what to search.

Entrance exam basics, plus creators we'd genuinely point a student toward, once we've made sure they're not quietly sponsored by someone with a stake in the answer.

Free prep resources, by exam

Everything below is something a student can start using today, for free. If a caution applies — a channel that skips something, or official sources beating YouTube — it's flagged before the list, not buried inside it.

JEE Main + JEE Advanced India · Engineering
Caution: this is the most saturated free-resource space in Indian ed-tech, and the real risk is decision fatigue rather than scarcity. Pick one spine channel plus a couple of subject specialists, not ten random ones. Student forums like Careers360 and Quora flag that some free channels teach shortcuts that fall apart on harder Advanced-level questions, so cross-check anything tricky against NCERT or PYQs.
Full-syllabus "spine" channels (pick one)
CreatorBest forNotes
Physics Wallah / JEE Wallah (Alakh Pandey)All 3 subjects, beginner–advancedLargest free JEE ecosystem in India; started the "free coaching" movement.
Unacademy JEELive classes, PYQ-based sessionsEducators include Aman Dhattarwal, Naman Agarwal, Shivani Verma, Sachin Rana.
Vedantu JEEInteractive live classesEducators include Vineet Khatri, Himanshu Pandey.
Etoos EducationStructured, coaching-institute styleLong-running, Kota-based.
Physics specialists
  • Physics Galaxy (Ashish Arora) — deep conceptual + Olympiad-level, ideal for Advanced.
  • NV Sir (Nitin Vijay) — strong fundamentals-first approach. (search his name on YouTube — couldn't verify one official link.)
  • Pradeep Kshetrapal — chapter-wise problem-solving, long-established (300K+ subs). (search on YouTube.)
  • Namo Kaul — well-regarded for Main + Advanced physics. (search on YouTube.)
Chemistry specialists
  • eSaral — strong PCM conceptual base.
  • ATP STAR Chemistry — Kota-level strategies, shortcuts.
  • Gabbar Singh Tutorial — chemistry-specific, long-running. (search on YouTube.)
  • Chemistry by PW — full Organic/Inorganic/Physical coverage. (part of the Physics Wallah channel family above.)
Maths specialists
  • Mohit Tyagi — widely called the go-to free Maths channel for Advanced; IIT Delhi graduate.
  • Neha Agrawal (Mathematically Inclined) — shortcuts and Main-specific strategy.
  • MathonGo — crash courses + PYQ breakdowns.
  • NM Sir (PW) — Coordinate Geometry & Trigonometry speed-building. (part of the Physics Wallah channel family above.)
Free platforms beyond YouTube
  • NCERT textbooks (Class 11–12) — the actual syllabus foundation.
  • NTA official website — free previous-year JEE Main papers.
  • MathonGo.com / eSaral.com — free PYQ banks and mock tests.
  • Khan Academy — beginner-friendly concept videos.
BITSAT India · BITS Pilani
Reminder: BITSAT uniquely tests English Proficiency + Logical Reasoning, which most JEE-focused channels skip entirely. Search for BITSAT-specific English/LR playlists separately, ideally in the last 3–4 weeks before the exam.
  • MathonGo (Anup Sir) — BITSAT-specific crash courses, PYQ breakdowns, attempt-order strategy.
  • Harshal — run by an actual BITS Pilani student; syllabus breakdowns, exam-pattern explanations. (search "Harshal BITSAT" on YouTube.)
  • Unacademy — posts BITSAT-tagged "most expected questions" playlists.
  • Vora Classes — has run free BITSAT crash-course livestreams (search "BITSAT crash course Vora Classes").
VITEEE, MET, SRMJEEE, COMEDK India · Private engineering
These overlap heavily with the JEE Main syllabus (roughly 65–75%), so a JEE Physics/Chemistry/Maths channel forms your base layer.
  • Several creators run joint "VITEEE/COMEDK/MET/BITSAT" live Q&A series since syllabi overlap — search these exam names together on YouTube (regional creators also run these Feb–May each year).
  • CrackRank and similar test-series platforms pair free YouTube content with free/paid mock tests for VITEEE and COMEDK. (search "CrackRank" — couldn't verify one official link.)
  • Official exam websites — VITEEE, COMEDK UGET (Manipal MET and SRMJEEE: search their name + "official site") — publish free previous-year papers, genuinely more useful than YouTube here: VITEEE is speed-based with shorter questions than JEE, COMEDK sits closer to Karnataka PU-board difficulty, and MET/SRMJEEE both run distinct question banks worth practicing directly.

WBJEE (West Bengal)

No single dominant WBJEE-only mega-channel exists. Most aspirants layer JEE Main-level content (Physics Wallah, Vedantu, eSaral) on top of WBJEE-specific PYQ practice, since the syllabus is effectively a subset of JEE Main. Prioritize the official WBJEE Board's released previous-year papers — third-party WBJEE-specific channels are thin.

TS EAPCET / AP EAPCET (formerly EAMCET)

Tests Intermediate (state board)-level content, not full JEE-level difficulty — generic JEE channels often pitch content too advanced. Official portal: AP EAPCET (search "TS EAPCET" for Telangana's; older relevant content is archived under "EAMCET"). Sri Chaitanya, Narayana, and Sri Gayatri — originally coaching brands — now post substantial free live-class content targeted at the Telangana/AP Intermediate syllabus that EAPCET actually tests.

CUET (UG) India · Central universities
CUET spans NCERT Class 11–12 content across many domain subjects. Treat YouTube as revision/strategy support layered on top of NCERT textbooks, which remain the actual primary source material.

ESAT, TMUA & STEP UK · Cambridge / Imperial admissions tests
These are lower-volume on YouTube compared to Indian/US exams. The genuinely best free resources here are official — lead with official links, using YouTube purely as supplementary material.
ESAT & TMUA — official platforms (start here)
  • esat-tmua.ac.uk — free Test Specification, "Notes on Logic and Proof," full past papers (2016–2024), specimen tests, and a timed practice test that mirrors the real exam interface.
  • TMUA Academy — free structured guides: Paper 1 vs Paper 2 strategy, timing techniques, scoring breakdowns.
  • LumiExams — free TMUA past papers with worked solutions, sourced from official materials.

YouTube: search "TMUA past paper walkthrough" for UK maths tutors' worked-solution videos; the Oxford MAT livestream is useful for the Mathematics 2 component ESAT shares with MAT.

STEP — official platforms (start here)
  • STEP Support Programme — Cambridge Faculty of Mathematics' own free programme: 25 Foundation modules plus dedicated STEP 2/3 modules, self-paced over roughly 6 months.
  • Underground Mathematics (DfE-funded, Cambridge-based) — free past STEP questions with fully worked solutions.
  • "Advanced Problems in Mathematics" by Stephen Siklos — free PDF, the classic STEP prep text, directly recommended by Cambridge.

YouTube: search "STEP maths preparation" or "STEP past paper walkthrough" for Cambridge-tutor-run strategy and worked-solution videos.

TOLC, EJU & TestAS Italy · Japan · Germany
These have essentially no dominant YouTube creator scene — prep here runs almost entirely on official past papers and practice platforms.

IELTS Global · English proficiency
Official test partner resources
  • IELTS.org sample questions — official practice for Academic, General Training, and Life Skills tests.
  • British Council practice tests — free practice tests, prep apps, and format guidance.
  • Computer Familiarisation Test — full-length experience for computer-based IELTS (Listening, Reading, Writing).
  • IDP IELTS Preparation Hub — free materials, webinars, expert guidance, plus the IELTS by IDP app.
Mock tests & practice platforms
  • OneIELTS — 100+ full computer-based mock tests, 400+ section tests, AI scoring for Writing/Speaking.
  • Free IELTS Resources (FI) — curated official practice links, study plans, sample papers, plus one free writing review.
Skill-specific
  • 35 Band 9 Model Essays (ieltspodcast.com) — high-scoring Task 2 model answers, reviewed by former examiners.
  • IELTS Liz — writing, speaking, and weekly tips lessons covering both Academic and General Training.
  • Official Band Descriptors — public guide to how examiners score Speaking 0–9.
Expert support
  • Free IELTS Masterclass (IDP India) — live sessions covering all four modules, with interactive Q&A.
TOEFL Global · English proficiency (2026 format)
TOEFL underwent significant changes in January 2026, including a new 1–6 band scoring scale and new task types. Everything below is selected for relevance to the updated format.
Official ETS resources
  • TOEFL TestReady Portal — free full-length practice test with AI scoring, a daily "Activity of the Day," and a tailored study plan tool.
  • TOEFL iBT Interactive Sample — a digital preview of the real test interface and question types.
  • TOEFL Go! app — official ETS content, rubrics, and AI scoring aligned with the actual test.
  • edX — "The Insider's Guide" — free self-paced course by ETS experts, covering all four sections.
Comprehensive prep platforms
  • Magoosh — free practice test built from licensed official ETS questions, scores on both legacy and new band scales.
  • Gabble.ai — free trial with criterion-by-criterion Speaking and sentence-level Writing feedback.
  • TestGlider — full mock tests with instant scoring and speaking-shadowing exercises.
Skill-focused practice (once official mocks are exhausted)
  • Wikipedia / Simple English Wikipedia — passage-length reading practice on science, history, social science.
  • Scientific American 60-Second Science, TED-Ed, Oxford University Podcasts — listening comprehension practice.
  • Purdue OWL — the gold standard for academic writing conventions and grammar exercises.
Vocabulary & community
  • PrepScholar's 327-word list, Magoosh's vocabulary flashcards app, and Magoosh's free 1- and 3-month study schedules.
  • r/ToeflAdvice — unofficial community sharing experiences and tips for the 2026 format.
